## Summary
Business Wire press release republished on The AI Journal — Infigo's official 2025 numbers and named US deployment wins. Most valuable for: confirmed customer names with deployment specifics (LPI church bulletins, Superior Packaging on 51 HP Site Flow storefronts), and Infigo's own framing of dev team size (28 specialists, ~half of total headcount).

## Key takeaways

**Growth & market metrics (Infigo's own numbers, 2025):**
- 18.2% YoY growth in 2025.
- 34 new clients onboarded since fiscal year start (May 2025).
- 18 of those 34 = US-based.
- ~60% of all 2025 new customers came from North America (US + Canada).
- 70% of customers operate in B2B environments.
- General commercial print = fastest-growing segment.
- Biweekly release cadence (Infigo's own claim — "a rare cadence in the industry").

**Named US customer deployments (third-party verifiable since BW is the wire-of-record):**
- **LPi (Liturgical Publications)** — one of the largest church-bulletin printers in the US. Infigo replaced legacy systems for weekly production serving 4,000+ churches nationally. Went fully live November 2025.
- **Superior Packaging and Finishing** — pharma / financial / regulated industries. Integrated Infigo with HP Site Flow to power all B2B storefronts. **51 live storefronts** across complex customer environments. Useful benchmark for multi-storefront deployments at scale.

**Strategic moves:**
- Reseller agreement with printIQ covering Australia and New Zealand — meaning in ANZ printIQ now sells Infigo licenses, deepening the partnership beyond a tech integration.
- 28 dedicated developers (Infigo's framing — "nearly half" of total team).

**Quotable Douglas Gibson (CEO/Founder):**
- "Printers that fail to adopt software platforms risk being forced out of the market within the next five to ten years."
- US specifically: "Many providers are still operating with manual processes that don't scale. As volume increases and turnaround expectations tighten, automation has become mission-critical to reducing manual effort, minimizing errors, and enabling providers to grow without adding headcount."
